text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Portugal joined Germany and voted against the entry of Italian carrency Lira in the Economic Monetary System (EMS).
- Ford and Volkswagen AutoEuropa joint venture at Palmela may have to stop its car assembly line if French lorry drivers strike continues. AutoEuropa will be out of stocks by Wednesday.

- Portuguese electricity company EDP paid around 700 dollars per consumer for Brasilian company Electricidade de Rio de Janeiro. Recently Electricite de France paid 1,200 dollars in similar operation.
- The Competition Council should issue its view on the privatisation of tobacco company Tabaqueira by the end of the week.

- Public opinion in some countries was amongst a number of potential threats to the European Union's plans for monetary union, European Monetary Institute chairman Alexandre Lamfalussy says in interview.
- Independent TVI television station wants to reduce capital 66 percent as part of recovery plan.
- Government intends to cut defence industry jobs. The sector's 6,500 workers are alarmed.
- Social Security system requires all Portuguese to sign up again by July 1997.
- Brussels approved Portuguese infrastructure projects for capturing, supplying and treatment of water involving 114 billion escudos, a source close to the Environment Ministry told the paper.
